mean.name: Mean Imputation
mean.description: Fills missing values with the average value of the column.
mean.conditions: Suitable only for continuous numeric data that is normally distributed and contains no significant outliers.

median.name: Median Imputation
median.description: Fills missing values with the middle value of the sorted column.
median.conditions: Recommended for skewed numeric distributions and columns with outliers.

mode.name: Mode Imputation
mode.description: Fills missing values with the most frequent value in the column.
mode.conditions: Best suited for categorical/nominal columns or discrete numeric columns with small ranges.

knn.name: K-Nearest Neighbors Imputation
knn.description: Uses similarity metrics to impute missing values based on neighboring observations.
knn.conditions: More accurate but computationally expensive. Suitable for low-to-medium dataset sizes.

standardization.name: Standardization (Z-score Normalization)
standardization.description: Scales data to have a mean of 0 and a standard deviation of 1.
standardization.conditions: Required for algorithms that assume normally distributed data (linear models, SVMs, neural networks).

minmax.name: Min-Max Scaling
minmax.description: Rescales data to a fixed range, usually 0 to 1.
minmax.conditions: Useful for algorithms that do not assume distribution shapes (KNNs, neural networks) and where exact bounds are known.

robust.name: Robust Scaling
robust.description: Scales data using the median and IQR, making it robust to outliers.
robust.conditions: Highly recommended when numerical columns contain significant outliers.

onehot.name: One-Hot Encoding
onehot.description: Creates binary columns for each unique category label.
onehot.conditions: Best for nominal categorical features with low cardinality (<30 unique values).

ordinal.name: Ordinal Encoding
ordinal.description: Maps categories to integers based on an ordered scale.
ordinal.formula: f(c_k) = k \text{ where } c_1 < c_2 < ... < c_m
ordinal.conditions: Required for categorical features that have an inherent order (e.g., educational grade, rating).

target.name: Target Encoding
target.description: Replaces categorical values with the mean target value for that category.
target.conditions: Recommended for high-cardinality nominal columns to avoid feature explosion.
